Strike table cells through

Source: R/table.R
pub_strikeout.Rd

Strikes cells through, e.g. excluded measurements or superseded values. Every output format shows them struck through. Like other cell properties, this survives huxtable's rbind(), cbind() and [.

Usage

pub_strikeout(ht, row, col)

Arguments

ht

A huxtable, e.g. from pub_table().

row, col

Rows and columns as in huxtable's setters such as huxtable::set_bold(): indices, names, logical vectors, huxtable::everywhere or huxtable::final(). Rows include the header rows (see pub_table()). Default: all.

Value

ht with the cells struck through.

Details

huxtable has no strikeout property, so the cells become Markdown cells (huxtable::markdown()) that hold their display text (see pub_cell_text()) between ~~. Therefore:

  • The text is fixed when the cells are struck through (a later change of their number format does not apply), so strike through last.

  • Empty cells stay unchanged.

  • Markdown characters in the text are escaped, and each line is struck through.

  • In cells that are Markdown already, each line is struck through as a whole after its block markers: ~~A~~ and B becomes ~~A and B~~ and "# A\n\n- b" becomes "# ~~A~~\n\n- ~~b~~".

See also

pub_table()

Examples

df <- airquality[1:3, c("Day", "Ozone", "Wind")]
excluded <- c(FALSE, TRUE, FALSE)
ht <- pub_table(df, digits = c(Wind = 1))
rows <- pub_table_rows(ht)$body[excluded]
ht <- huxtable::set_text_color(ht, rows, huxtable::everywhere, "grey")
ht <- pub_strikeout(ht, rows)
pub_cell_text(ht)
#>      [,1]    [,2]     [,3]     
#> [1,] "Day"   "Ozone"  "Wind"   
#> [2,] "1"     "41"     "7.4"    
#> [3,] "~~2~~" "~~36~~" "~~8.0~~"
#> [4,] "3"     "12"     "12.6"
